newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends up, market awaits mini-band drop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends up, market awaits mini-band drop.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.07 percent to close at 1.0426 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, with players awaiting a new lowering in the real-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The current mini-band, between 1.0425 and 1.0475, was set Jan 15 by the Central Bank.
Some players expected the Central Bank would take advantage of the calmness in the market today due to the Martin Luther King Jr holiday in the United States to lower the mini-band.
Because the change did not take place today, expectations are that the Central Bank will move the mini-band Tuesday, dealers said.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.34 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.50 percent and 0.65 percent.
The real's rise was due to a strong inflow of dollars, dealers said. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a Monday surplus of $200 million.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real closed steady at 1.0485 per dollar. In the illegal parallel market, the real dropped 0.46 to end at 1.100 per greenback.
